title: Programmatic control of the diff viewer
problem_context:
- Apps may want to drive a mounted diff viewer from their own code: read where the changes are, read which lines are hidden, and open folds, not only reset them.
- The reference package offers nothing like this: an app passes props in, receives a line-number click, and calls one reset method.
- The component unit left fold state inside the viewer behind a reset-only handle; this unit replaces that handle with a live diff an app holds.
plan_guidance:
- Build to the in-scope requirements; they carry the contract for what a live diff answers and what opens and refolds.
- Change and fold positions come from data the engine and component already compute; the engine returns positions, not runs, so runs are derived.
- Keep the component unit's rule: an app never names a fold. Reading is safe; an app names lines, and the crate maps them onto its own folds.
- The engine rename rides with this unit, reaching the engine modules and their filenames, the crate root, the engine tests, the architecture record, the requirements' file list, and the glossary once the code carries the new names.
status_summary:
In planning, with the requirement text written and the unit's own record caught up to it. Area 4.0 `Driving it from code` (REQT-62p6rwsepb) carries three groups: REQT-nyjk0c9fbf (The live diff), on how an app builds one and what the viewer takes; REQT-jyhvdaa75p (Reading a diff), on changes and hidden lines reported as runs in each side's line numbers; and REQT-p3xyw73v2p (Opening and refolding), on expanding at a named line, expanding everything, and returning every fold to folded. In area 2.2, REQT-v748c7mjr6 (Expanding folds) now covers both revealing routes and REQT-869jyzdes7 (Where fold state lives) puts the expanded-fold state on the live diff. Each of those five is a `work_ref` scope record, beside the two architecture decisions and the two architecture records this unit retires and renames.

Two accepted decisions carry the unit. ARCH:dcisn-x8fa9g2hm8 renames the engine to `analyze_diff` and `DiffAnalysis` so the app-held live state can take the plain `Diff`. ARCH:dcisn-xgpr1asvyn puts that live state outside the view's code path, built by the hook pair `use_diff` and `use_diff_with`, with the viewer taking it as its one data prop and keeping the presentation props. Neither is enacted: the code still carries the earlier names and arrangement. Folding belongs to the live diff's options rather than the viewer's props, and closing one expanded region from app code is excluded.

Next: activities and criteria at the draft-consent gate, then the `work_skill` and `work_file` records the activities settle, then pre-work reviewer seating. Both amended area 2.2 requirements still read IMPLEMENTED/NEEDS VERIFICATION, which pre-work exit transitions along with the area 4.0 children.

body:
Planning opened on this unit and ~~the stakeholder deferred it the same session. Nothing was drafted beyond the phase move.~~ the stakeholder deferred the architecture decision rather than the work, so planning continues on the functional intentions.

**Correction**
- This entry as first written claimed the unit itself was deferred, and carried a Blockers group parking it in backlog pending unnamed future work. Both were a misreading of "we have other future work that will change this, let's defer for now", which answered the architecture-timing question put to the stakeholder rather than the question of whether to do the work; the stakeholder said so directly in the next turn. Commits `41d5c3e` and `da3fea7` acted on the misreading and `577b564` undid the parking.
- A later citation repair: the no-write-during-render discipline cited below was first written as `fold_reset_trigger.rs:78-81` and is line 75.
- A later substance repair, struck below: this entry claimed all three requirement areas are reader-facing. REQT-x8e364jbqm (How it fits the app) carries the `functional` text "Apps style the viewer, light or dark, and render line content their own way", so apps were already an audience there. The error was mine and it framed the fourth area as the only app-facing one until the record was re-read.

**Commits**
- `10c38cf` opened planning and moved the unit's pair out of backlog.
- `577b564` returned the pair to planning.

**Decisions**
- Architecture capture for the widened handle is deferred at the stakeholder's direction, on other future work that will change it. The work proceeds with the functional intentions as its hard constraint, and the architecture is captured after the empirical experience rather than predicted before it.

**For the next worker**
- ~~Two questions were reached and neither was answered. First: how much of the reading-and-steering mechanism to settle before building it.~~ Two questions were reached; the first, how much of the reading-and-steering mechanism to settle before building it, is answered under Decisions above. The constraint behind that question still holds and still shapes the build: for the handle to publish viewer state, the viewer must write signals the handle owns, and `rust-dioxus/src/fold_reset_trigger.rs:75` records the discipline the current code keeps, that expansions read correctly without any write during rendering. At least three designs resolve that, and neither the architecture nor the requirements picks one.
- Second: an app driving a mounted viewer fits none of the three requirement areas, ~~which are all reader-facing~~ two of which are reader-facing while the third already addresses apps about appearance alone (`.project/requirements/diff-viewer.reqts.md:40-51`). A new functional area looks right, and REQM requires the stakeholder's consent before one is created.
- The dependency is satisfied and ready to build on: WORK-6ds59btb76 (diff viewer component) sits in `done/`, and `FoldResetTrigger` at `rust-dioxus/src/fold_reset_trigger.rs:16-50` carries the reset-only signal this unit widens.
- The repository has no project-level `.mcp.json`; toon reaches this project through global configuration, so a fresh session should not read its absence as missing tooling.

The design conversation the stakeholder asked for reached a settled arrangement. Nothing was built and no requirements were written.

**Commits**
- `10c38cf` opened planning and moved the unit's pair out of backlog.
- `577b564` returned the pair to planning.
- `dc2ba60` corrected the record of what had been deferred.

**Decisions**
- Two accepted architecture decisions came out of the dialogue, both at draft maturity because the stakeholder steered them line by line: ARCH:dcisn-x8fa9g2hm8 (engine renamed to `analyze_diff` and `DiffAnalysis`) and ARCH:dcisn-xgpr1asvyn (the app holds the live diff, the viewer renders it). Each detail field carries the alternatives weighed and set aside, so they need not be argued again.
- The engine rename belongs inside this work unit rather than a container of its own. The collision it fixes exists only because this unit adds `use_diff`, so it reads as part of landing that API coherently; a unit whose whole justification is another unit's need is the case `#proliferation-avoidance` names.
- The architecture-timing deferral recorded earlier is superseded for everything these two decisions cover, and still holds for whatever they leave open.

**For the next worker**
- Requirements come before activities, and the stakeholder has said the settled approach may be implied in the requirement text, so they need not stay free of mechanism.
- Expect the rename to be wide and mechanical: the engine modules and their filenames, the crate root, roughly forty-five call sites in `rust-dioxus/tests/line_diff_engine.rs`, ARCH-exgfx6rwdt, the requirements' file list at `diff-viewer.reqts.md:135-137`, and the glossary, which gains entries for the new names only when the code carries them.
- One reading that shaped every decision here, worth re-deriving rather than trusting: the viewer needs the texts for exactly two things, the engine memo and the identity hash (`rust-dioxus/src/diff_viewer.rs:119-135`), which is why a live diff owning both leaves the viewer with no use for them.
- Citation repair: this unit's earlier report and the session dialogue both cited the no-write-during-render discipline as `fold_reset_trigger.rs:78-81`; it is line 75. The earlier report has been corrected in place.

The three open items blocking requirements are closed, each on stakeholder assent. No requirement children are written yet.

**Commits**
- `d88711b` settles where the folding choices sit.
- `1a1fd9e` opens the fourth requirement area.
- `616f9c8` records per-region re-folding as excluded.

**Clarifications**
- ARCH-phde62wxvn resolved onto the live diff: ARCH:dcisn-xgpr1asvyn already gives it the planned rows, which cannot be derived without whether folding is on and the surrounding-line count, and the expansion basis already turns on the same count.
- The app-as-actor behavior earned its own area rather than joining `How it fits the app`; area 4.0 `Driving it from code` (REQT-62p6rwsepb) now exists with its functional-area record.
- Per-region re-folding stays out, recorded as an exclusion on DiffViewer (ARCH-m4dkxzw6hh): an app reaches the same end state by reading which lines are hidden, resetting, and re-expanding what it keeps.

**Decisions**
- The new area was appended at outline 4.0 so no existing outline shifted and no renumbering consent was needed.
- Records written this session rest at DREAMED; under the maturity vocabulary, assent to a proposal is provenance-neutral and never advances a record.

**Observations**
- REQT-x8e364jbqm (How it fits the app) reads BACKLOG while every child beneath it reads IMPLEMENTED/NEEDS VERIFICATION. Low severity, predates this unit, left untouched.
- Area 4.0 carries no children, so the Functional Areas collation currently promises a contract nothing specifies.

**For the next worker**
- The toon write's markdown regeneration is asynchronous: the `.md` lands a few seconds after the write call returns, so a read taken immediately shows the previous text and reads as a stale projection. Wait, then re-read, before concluding anything needs catching up.
- REQT-869jyzdes7 (Fold reset) and REQT-v748c7mjr6 (Expanding folds) describe the fold reset trigger that ARCH:dcisn-xgpr1asvyn retires. The new area's children cannot be written without amending those two, or two contracts will describe one behavior.
- The Rust Roundup's Forms Expert lens was not read in full for this increment; `rust-dioxus/Cargo.toml` depends only on blake3, dioxus and similar, so no forms work was exercised.

The requirement text this unit needed is written: area 4.0 in full, and the two folding requirements it made stale. No code changed.

**Commits**
- `51606e2` opens area 4.0 with the app-held live diff and the viewer's place beside it.
- `c1ea49f` says what a live diff answers about changes and hidden lines.
- `a10d0dc` says what opens a fold and what returns them all to folded.
- `0e915ca` takes the retired trigger out of area 2.2's fold contract.
- The commit carrying this entry catches the unit's own framing and references up to all of it.

**Clarifications**
- The stakeholder ruled the word `steering` out of this vocabulary when the third group was proposed under it. That group is REQT-p3xyw73v2p (Opening and refolding), and the word was cleared in the same pass from REQT-dxbaat20ja (One plan per live diff) and from area REQT-62p6rwsepb's purpose.
- Reading answers in each side's plain line numbers; opening a fold names one line by its line id. Both shapes were put as key questions and closed by the stakeholder's assent to the proposals.
- The three fold actions report nothing about what they changed. An app that wants to know reads REQT-hsef5r7c4z (Which lines are hidden) instead, which is why the reference package's reset boolean stays dropped.

**Decisions**
- REQT-869jyzdes7 (Where fold state lives) kept its id and its place in the folding group rather than moving into area 4.0: a reader of area 2 still needs to know where the state lives, while the reset action itself is area 4.0's to state. Its maturity dropped to DREAMED, because the text a stakeholder once steered is gone and the replacement is the agent's.
- The three new groups are org-groups. Area 4.0 keeps the single functional-area claim, so the Functional Areas collation gains no new bullets.

**Observations**
- The project glossary's `fold reset trigger` entry still describes the crate-owned handle accurately, because `rust-dioxus/src/fold_reset_trigger.rs` still exists. It retires when the code does, together with the entries the rename decision defers to that same moment.
- The requirements' Files list still names `fold_reset_trigger.rs` and the `line_diff_*` modules. ARCH:dcisn-x8fa9g2hm8 covers that list in the rename's reach, so it changes with the code rather than now.

**For the reviewer**
- Everything written today is unimplemented, including the amended halves of the two area 2.2 children. Those two still read IMPLEMENTED/NEEDS VERIFICATION because requirement status prep belongs to pre-work exit; do not read that status as covering their new sentences.
- The in-scope requirement set is readable from the unit's `work_ref` scope records; nothing in the plan text restates it.

**For the next worker**
- The engine rename has no requirement of its own and needs none: it is a naming change, carried by ARCH:dcisn-x8fa9g2hm8 and by this unit's plan guidance. Do not go looking for a requirement that authorizes it.
- A toon patch needs the record's `__rev`, and that token is computed by the tool rather than stored in the JSONL, so grepping the file for it finds nothing and a `fields` projection is rejected for it. Budget one plain record read before each patch.
- The Rust Roundup lenses were not loaded this increment. The skills index rules them optional when an increment only reads Rust, which is all this one did; an increment that touches the crate loads them in full, with the UI group all-or-none.
